reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate and does not fit the budget. (1) Premise check, measured with gp: K_0 over Z has j=-1/433 (disc -433), while the canonical lift has j=-3375. j(K_0)-(-3375) has 2-adic valuation 1, so they agree only mod 2 and K_0/Z is NOT its own canonical lift even mod 4. At mod 4 any Z/4-lift gives a homomorphic odd-order section T, so the experiment is still definable, but 'canonical lift' and the Voloch-Walker/Finotti degree bound cannot be assumed and must be measured. (2) ANF-degree arm is near-vacuous and is a strawman. T is Galois-equivariant on a curve defined over F_2, so x_1 should be a universal F in F_2(x_0) with no dependence on n. Its Boolean degree is then bounded by the max popcount of its exponents, constant in n by construction, unless F has 1/x_0^k terms. Inversion has weight n-1, so the real discriminating question is Laurent terms vs polynomial, not the n-grid. The false-branch prediction 'ANF degree >= n/2' is only reachable via inverse terms. Computing the ANF needs the 2^n truth table; n=23 is 8.4M GR(4,23) scalar multiplications in pure python, which is infeasible in 18 min. (3) The decisive quantity is not tested. B_w = {x_0 : F(x_0) in V} is an implicit set. It has no ell-bit parametrisation, because that needs F^{-1}, which generically has degree about n. The descended system therefore has m*n Boolean unknowns, versus m*ell for a subspace base, and about n+m(n-ell) equations of degree >= 2 (more if deg F >= 3). The proposed arm 'd_F vs an equal-size subspace base' compares systems with different variable counts and different geometry. A d_F that does not grow at ell=3..5 is also trivial: subspace d_F at fixed small ell is bounded in n anyway, and the programme measures D = ceil(ell/2)+4 at m=3, which depends on ell. The scaling-relevant regime is ell ~ n/m', not ell=3..5. (4) Carry layer: T is an injective homomorphism on the odd-order subgroup, and odd-order points are Zariski dense in E(Fbar). So the lifted-S_{m+1} identity mod 4 holds identically on S_{m+1}=0 over Fbar, hence C lies in rad(S_{m+1}), i.e. C = S_{m+1}*h for squarefree S. Weil descent is a ring map, so the n carry equations are ideal-redundant. This is a proof sketch, not a measurement. Expected rank gain is 0, and 'free carry equations' is false by this argument. The experiment should confirm it with a rank test, but a positive d_F gain would contradict the argument and flag a bug. (5) Yield arm has no power. B ~ d*2^ell = 8..32*d, B^m/r ~ 1e-3 per target, and 50 targets give about 0 expected hits. Yield must be counted as exact decomposition counts over enumerated B^m sums versus size-matched random-set and subspace nulls, and the monodromy closure says mean yield equals random anyway, so 'yield = random' is a sanity control, not evidence. (6) Budget: 5 n x 3 ell x 2 m x 50 targets = 1500 msolve cells on 46-69 Boolean variables in 18 CPU-min = 0.7 s/cell, not credible; F4 on 69 Boolean unknowns blows up. Metric type is fine (rank, degree, F4 max-degree and matrix dims are structural), but wall time must stay out of it. Net: the idea is cheaply falsifiable on the carry-rank and variable-count points, and the fix keeps the same question while making it decisive and runnable.
fix: Replace the grid by four cheap, decisive stages, all pure python/numpy/gp/msolve, about 10 CPU-min total. (A) Derive F once, not per n. Implement GR(4,n)=Z4[t]/(f) arithmetic with affine K_0 addition (inverse via Newton or Hensel from F_{2^n}). For n=11 and 13 compute T(P)=[2^n*a]Q with a=2^{-n} mod odd|E|, and read x_1 in Witt coordinates, x=[x_0]+2*x_1. Fit x_1 = F(x_0) with F in F_2[x_0, 1/x_0] by F_2 linear algebra over exponents |k|<=64, then verify exactly on all other points and on n=17,19,23 samples. Also cross-check on two other Z/4 lifts (a6=1 plus 2*c, c in {1,..}) to show the dependence on the lift. Record terms, deg F, number of inverse terms, and popcount-ANF degree. Then run a 20-point check at n=131 with gp or python big ints: 131 doublings in GR(4,131), compare to F. This is the only n-scaling statement that transfers to 131 (F universal => deg constant for all n); everything else in the plan is toy. If F has 1/x_0^k terms, ANF degree = n-1 and the idea is closed on stage A. (B) Carry redundancy as a rank test, not a degree test. Build the m=2 (S_3) and m=3 (S_4) descended system over F_2 with unknown x_0's as n-bit vectors (n=11,13,17) with only the mod-2 equations plus field equations, and a second system with the mod-4 lifted-S carry equations added, using x_1=F(x_0). Compare the msolve -g 2 reduced GB (leading ideal / HF) and the F4 max-degree table (msolve -v 2) between the two. Prediction if the sketch is right: identical ideals; reject the idea's carry premise if the ideals differ. Also run a cheap 'zero-sum' exhaustive check on n=11 (all x_0 pairs), reducing C mod S_3, to check C in (S_3). (C) Matched-variable-count solve test. Compare, at identical unknown-bit count and identical number of equations, three bases: V-subspace (m*ell unknowns); B_w implicit (m*n unknowns plus m*(n-ell) equations of degree deg F); and a size-matched random-preimage base {x : G(x) in V} with G a random permutation-polynomial of the same degree as F (null arm for 'is F special'). Cells: n in {11,13,17}, m in {2,3}, ell = round(n/(m+1)) and round(n/m) (the scaling regime ell ~ n/m', not 3..5), 10 targets/cell, msolve -g 2 -v 2 with a 20 s per-cell cap. Report F4 max degree, last matrix size, number of unknown bits, and timeouts, so a timeout counts as 'degree not bounded'. Also report the actual size |B_w| per V (preimage multiplicities). Prediction if true: B_w max degree <= max degree of the random-G null and does not grow with n at fixed ell/n. Prediction if false: B_w tracks the random-G null (F gives no structure) and exceeds the subspace baseline at every cell, with unknown-bit count mn vs m*ell as the cause. The expected outcome is 'false'. (D) Yield as exact counts. For n=11,13 enumerate all B^m sums for the three bases and count distinct decomposable targets and total decompositions, against Poisson mean; accept 'yield = random' only to within 3 sigma, not 5%. Add the scaling argument to the record: B*D^2 << N requires D=poly(n) with B ~ 2^{n/m'}, but B_w needs m*n unknowns unless F^{-1} has low degree. State that in the verdict file, and require stage C to measure deg(F^{-1}) on the toy as the polynomial of the inverse map over n=11,13 (inverse degree about n would confirm the obstruction). Classification stays 'relabelling' unless stage C shows B_w beats the random-G null and the subspace baseline in variable-normalised terms.
